{{nihongo|'''Mioya Shrine'''|水祖神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Oki Province]].

'''Mioya Shrine''' (みおやじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Tenjinbara, Minatomachi, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|Q1205039|qid=Q1205039}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|Q735735|qid=Q735735}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking}} it was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The shrine enshrines the following two deities<ref name="Explanation plaque">Explanation plaque on the shrine grounds.</ref>.
; Principal deity
:* {{ill|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|qid=Q8191796|lt=Mizuhanome-no-Kami}}
; Associated deity
:* {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}}

This shrine is identified with the “Mioya Shrine” listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}, but this identification dates only from after the late Edo-period work *Oki Kokishū*. Medieval and early modern sources instead describe it as a shrine dedicated to {{ill|Tenjin faith|Q66890725|qid=Q66890725|lt=Tenman Tenjin}} {{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Kami)|2000}}. This is understood to be because, at some point, Tenman Tenjin was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kanjō}} at Mioya Shrine, and as devotion to Tenman Tenjin increased, it became better known than the original Mioya Shrine deity {{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Kami)|2000}}. The associated deity Sugawara no Michizane corresponds to this Tenman Tenjin, and even today Mioya Shrine itself is commonly called “Tenjin-san” {{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Kami)|2000}}.

There is another shrine of the same name, Mioya Shrine, in Hatta Enokihara, Okinoshima Town; according to tradition, the deity of that shrine is said to have drifted to become the Mioya Shrine at Tenjinbara<ref>“Gokokuji Village,” *Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 33: Place Names of Shimane Prefecture*. Heibonsha, 1995.</ref>.

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
The date of foundation is unknown {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Records|1912}}. The hill behind the shrine buildings is also said to be an {{ill|Kofun|Q1141225|qid=Q1141225}}<ref name="Explanation plaque"/>{{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}.

In the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}, compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), “Mioya Shrine” is listed in {{ill|Oki Province|Q1063829|qid=Q1063829}} {{ill|Suki district|Q10920245|qid=Q10920245}}, and this shrine is identified with that entry {{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Kami)|2000}}. The *Oki Jinmyōchō* also records “Junior Fourth Rank, Mioya Myōjin,” but details of changes during the medieval period are unknown {{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Kami)|2000}}.

A ridge tag from {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenmon}} 22 ({{ill|1554|Q6570|qid=Q6570}}) refers to “Tenman Daijizai Tenjin,” and ridge tags from {{ill|Shōhō|Q1146192|qid=Q1146192}} 3 ({{ill|1646|Q6930|qid=Q6930}}) and {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 10 ({{ill|1670|Q7606|qid=Q7606}}) also describe it as a shrine dedicated to Tenman Tenjin {{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Kami)|2000}}. In addition, the *Inshū Shichō Gōki* from {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 7 ({{ill|1667|Q7588|qid=Q7588}}) and the *Inshūki* from {{ill|Jōkyō|Q1146221|qid=Q1146221}} 5 ({{ill|1688|Q7671|qid=Q7671}}) both record it as a Tenmangū {{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Kami)|2000}}. Later, beginning with the late Edo-period *Oki Kokishū*, which records the name “Gōso Shrine,” various works thereafter note that it should be identified with the “Mioya Shrine” of the *Engishiki* register {{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Kami)|2000}}.

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, the shrine name was fixed as “Mioya Shrine,” and in {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}) it was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} {{Sfn|Mioya Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}.
